title: OpenAI promised developers six months’ notice. GPT-4o users got three.
key_facts: OpenAI will retire GPT-4o, GPT-4o mini, GPT-4.1 and GPT-4.1 mini from its API on 14 Jan 2027, including dated snapshots and fine-tuned models built on them.
The notice went to developers on Wednesday (14 Oct 2026, by the article's timing), about three months ahead.
OpenAI's own policy promises at least six months' notice for generally available models, with exceptions for safety or compliance; no reason was given here.
The recommended replacement, GPT-6 Luna, costs $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens, but handles reasoning and tool calls differently.
Above 272,000 input tokens, input pricing doubles and output rises 50% for the whole request.
New self-serve fine-tuning jobs end on 6 Jan 2027.
The List models API now has a shutdown_date field.
Customers needing more time may arrange dedicated capacity with OpenAI sales.
quote_evidence: The three-month warning also falls short of OpenAI's own deprecation policy, which promises at least six months' notice for generally available models.
The policy allows exceptions for safety or compliance reasons, but there's no explanation for why GPT-4o and GPT-4.1 are getting only half that time.
OpenAI is retiring four GPT-4 models from its API on January 14, 2027.
why_it_matters_hint: Developers must migrate production apps in three months, half the notice OpenAI's policy promises.
notes: Article does not give the notice date explicitly; 'Wednesday' with a 15 Oct publication implies 14 Oct. Single outlet's reading of OpenAI's notice.
